_comment: The shipped Lightspeed Restaurant K-Series scenario, slice 1 of D-016 (konyklabs/roadmap#179).
Every id is written by hand in an obviously sequential pattern; the shapes are the vendor's,
the values are not copies of any real account's. seed/constants.py names each of them and
Shapes, all fetched 2026-10-29: businesses and businessLocations from apeLookupBusinesses and
location); the menu from apeMenuV2 in https://api-docs.lsk.lightspeed.app/source.json (one top-level
group of @type group, two menuItem entries with sku, productPrice, taxes, defaultTaxAmount,
defaultTaxPercentage, taxIncludedInPrice and an empty menuModifierGroups). Every menuEntry carries
@type because the document's oneOf is told apart by nothing else. The online-ordering tutorial
is why both items carry one. Prices and tax rates are JUDGMENT: one item tax-exclusive, one
tax-inclusive, and each tax amount is what the tax breakdown computes at quantity 1
Tokens are readable strings here (a human types them into curl); every token POST /oauth/token mints
is UUID-shaped, as both samples on the V1 authorization overview are. The full pair carries
financial-api and orders-api; the second access token carries financial-api only, so a 403 on an
Order and Pay read has something to be asserted with. Expiries come from the unit's clock at hydrate.
